overview.text: The Mother of God parish identifies the Descent into Hades as a traditional image of Holy Saturday and the Resurrection. It explicitly presents the composition as theological depiction, rather than an eyewitness description of an event someone observed and recorded.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph; About the Icon, paragraph 1

overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: Christ stands within a mandorla above the shattered gates of Hades, raising Adam and receiving Eve and the righteous. Broken locks, bars, and chains beneath Him express the destruction of death’s captivity. The source identifies Adam with the human race.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected icon from the Ferapontov Monastery is attributed in the file record to Dionisius and his workshop. It includes a company of the righteous around Christ and additional action below; the explanatory text addresses the shared type rather than cataloguing every figure.

sourceRefs.locator: File description and displayed historic reproduction

blocks.reason: Necessary English description of the selected historic artwork and its published object metadata; no new theological interpretation.

blocks.text: The parish reads Christ’s action as deliverance from the kingdom of death. His Resurrection is shown reaching the ancestral dead, while the broken gates visualize the victory proclaimed by the feast. The explanation identifies Christ’s death itself with His trampling of death.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph; About the Icon, paragraph 1

blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.
